stimulus.text: Paraphrase: At Yalta, in the Crimea, from February 4 to 11, 1945, Roosevelt, Churchill, and Stalin made the main decisions about postwar Europe. Germany would be divided into four zones of occupation, run by the United States, Britain, France, and the Soviet Union. Poland's borders would shift west, and a Soviet-backed government would rule at once, with a promise of free elections to follow. The Soviet Union would enter the war against Japan within three months of Germany's defeat, and in return it would gain the Kuril Islands, the southern half of Sakhalin Island, and railroad rights in Manchuria. The leaders also agreed to create a new United Nations, with a Security Council in which the great powers could block action.
stimulus.source_note: Original secondary summary drawn from Barron's Chapter 9 (Yalta Conference) and 5 Steps Chapter 24 (Yalta: Germany divided into four zones; free elections promised in Eastern Europe; Soviet Union to join the war against Japan).

source: original; stimulus drawn from book-grounded paraphrases, tables, and photographs (see source_note)
stem: How was Germany to be governed after its surrender, according to the Yalta agreements?

options.text: Divided into four occupation zones run by the Allies
Ruled as one country by a Soviet-chosen government
options.misconception: No single government ruled Germany after the surrender; each zone had its own military government.

options.text: Returned at once to a freely elected German government
options.misconception: No German national government existed until 1949, four years after the surrender.

options.text: Placed under the direct control of the United Nations
options.misconception: The United Nations had no power to govern Germany; the four occupying powers did.

rationales.A: The Yalta agreements divided Germany into four occupation zones, one run by each of the four powers. Background: Berlin, which lay inside the Soviet zone, was divided into four sectors as well.
rationales.B: Background from the books: no single government ruled Germany after the surrender; each zone had its own military government.
rationales.C: Background from the books: no German national government existed until 1949, four years after the surrender.
rationales.D: Background from the books: the United Nations had no power to govern Germany; the four occupying powers did.
rationales.general:
1. The stimulus says Germany would be divided into four zones of occupation.
2. The four powers were the United States, Britain, France, and the Soviet Union.
3. Background: Berlin was divided into four sectors as well, even though it lay inside the Soviet zone.
4. Each zone was run by its own military government until the Cold War split Germany in two.
Remember: occupation zones divide a defeated country among its conquerors.
